entries.source_title: Chaque/Tous les + [durée] = Each/every + [duration] (French Indefinite Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Contrasts chaque plus singular with tous les/toutes les plus plural, including multi-unit intervals; learners construct every two days and distinguish every two weeks from twice weekly.

entries.source_title: Même can mean "same", "itself", "very", "exact" and "precise" as an adjective, and "even" as an adverb in French
entries.evidence: Separately teaches agreeing same, post-noun exact day/place and quality itself, hyphenated self pronouns including polite singular vous-même, and invariable even; each distinction has a constrained item.

entries.source_title: Dernier = final/previous (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.evidence: Contrasts the preceding calendar period with the final member of an identified sequence, without universalizing the position rule; items construct last year/month and the final day of a course.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -u in French
entries.evidence: Shows -u/-ue/-us/-ues with unchanged spoken ending and contrasts the unrelated -eux family; learners supply feminine singular pointue and feminine plural têtues.

entries.source_title: Ancien = former/old (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.evidence: Teaches former status before a role noun and old/antique after an object noun, with contextual limits; exercises require both positions and plural agreement.

entries.source_title: Certain = specific / sure in French (adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.evidence: Distinguishes a particular unspecified address from a definite result; the tasks test pre-noun certaine and the meaning of post-noun certain.

entries.source_title: Better and better, worse and worse = de mieux en mieux, de pire en pire (Comparisons in French)
entries.evidence: Explains gradual change with de plus/moins en plus/moins, improving actions with de mieux en mieux, agreeing de meilleures en meilleures and deteriorating de pire en pire; learners construct both adjectival and adverbial progressions.

entries.source_title: Propre = own/clean (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.evidence: Pairs possessive plus pre-noun propre for ownership with post-noun propre for cleanliness; tasks construct both meanings with singular and plural referents.

entries.source_title: Plus... plus..., moins... moins... = the more...the more..., the less...the less... (comparisons with phrases)
entries.evidence: Teaches matching and mixed comparative clauses as linked changes without an English-style article; exercises build the intended less/more relationship and remove spurious le.

entries.source_title: Le/la/les plus and Le/la/les moins = The most and the least (Superlative with Adjectives in French)
entries.evidence: Shows article and adjective agreement when ranking distinct members, pre/post-noun placement and possessive replacement; constructed tasks give la plus calme and les moins chères.

entries.source_title: Vrai = real/true (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.evidence: Contrasts emphatic genuine status with factual truth while acknowledging contextual overlap; tasks specify a factually true story and an emphatically real problem.

entries.source_title: Supérieur à/Inférieur à (Irregular Comparatives in French)
entries.evidence: Teaches built-in comparison, adjective agreement and à rather than que without added plus; exercises test supérieur à and inférieur au with the required contraction.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of adjectives ending in -al in French
entries.evidence: Displays masculine -al/-aux and feminine -ale/-ales paradigms; exercises construct nationaux and originaux rather than applying feminine endings.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French adjectives ending in -al (exceptions)
entries.evidence: Teaches and separately exercises banal, bancal, fatal, natal and naval exceptions plus both accepted final/idéal/glacial plurals; distinguishes historical banaux as recognition from ordinary productive banals.

entries.source_title: Meilleur, mieux, pire / plus mauvais, plus mal = better, best, worse and worst in French (irregular comparatives and superlatives)
entries.evidence: Separates noun quality from action performance, gives full meilleur agreement and le mieux, accepts appropriate pire/plus mauvais variants, and exercises adjectival best as well as adverbial le plus mal.

entries.source_title: Cher= dear/expensive (French Adjectives that change meaning according to position)
entries.evidence: Explains affectionate pre-noun cher, price description after a noun/être, and cher à as emotional value; exercises include feminine agreement and the non-price construction.

entries.source_title: Quelque/quelques vs Un peu de/peu de = A couple/a few vs a bit of/few (French Indefinite Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Separates countable quelques from mass un peu de and scarce peu de, explicitly teaches singular quelque temps and de elision, and warns that quelques does not mean exactly two.

entries.source_title: Compound colour names and colour names derived from things are invariable (French Colour Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Contrasts agreeing simple colours with invariable compound and noun-based shades. Items individually exercise marron/orange/crème, rose/mauve/pourpre/écarlate/fauve/incarnat and compound bleu clair/bleu-vert/rose pâle.

entries.source_title: Some French adverbs end in -ément
entries.evidence: Provides a learned set rather than a false universal rule, then retrieves all ten named forms: précisément, profondément, énormément, intensément, aveuglément, communément, confusément, commodément, conformément and expressément.

entries.source_title: "Des" becomes " de/d' " in front of adjectives preceding nouns (French Articles)
entries.evidence: Teaches careful-written de/d' before freely preceding plural adjectives, contrasts post-noun placement and spoken usage, and preserves fixed des petits pois/des grands-parents. Items test de, d' and both named lexicalized exceptions.

entries.source_title: Animals names are often different for male, female and baby in French
entries.evidence: Article/gender-marked family vocabulary covers pets, livestock and poultry, with generic versus sex-specific adults and young animals. Thirty-five tasks retrieve every introduced family branch, irregular plurals and grammatical gender distinct from sex, including rabbits, geese and turkeys.

entries.source_title: Passer/se passer/se passer de - the different meanings of the verb "passer" in French
entries.evidence: Distinguishes passing through/spending time, events happening and doing without; full present and compound structures support items on se passe, se passer de, route par and pronominal past agreement.

entries.source_title: Differences between French and English usages - Passer un exam vs To pass an exam
entries.evidence: Separates sitting an exam from success, teaches both réussir un examen and réussir à un examen alongside rater/échouer à, and constrains items to the intended taking/result construction.

entries.source_title: Avoir un exam = To pass an exam (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.evidence: Teaches avoir son examen as contextual result talk, contrasts j'ai un examen demain, and supplies all six avoir-eu forms; tasks distinguish success from a scheduled exam.

entries.source_title: Passer can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Compares modern movement/visit être with direct-object avoir, including a time period as object, gives six-person patterns and subject agreement, and acknowledges intransitive variation rather than imposing an absolute.

entries.source_title: Expressing "to leave" with partir/laisser/quitter/sortir in French
entries.evidence: Provides all present forms, complement patterns and common past auxiliaries of four leaving verbs; exercises distinguish departing from, leaving a direct-object place, leaving something behind and taking something out.

entries.source_title: Using the compound past (Le Passé Composé) vs the present (Le Présent) in negative sentences with "depuis" (since/for) in French
entries.evidence: Contrasts a continuing changed habit/state with the absence of completed events up to now, explains possible viewpoint overlap, and constrains tasks by intended tense to avoid rejecting valid alternative readings.

entries.source_title: Avoir du mal à/avec = To have trouble, to struggle to/with (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.evidence: Teaches avoir du mal à plus infinitive versus avec plus noun, all present avoir persons and the contrast with physical avoir mal; exercises retrieve the verb phrase and both links.

entries.source_title: Using "faillir + [infinitive]" to say you almost did something in French
entries.evidence: Shows six-person avoir + failli and a direct following infinitive, explains the near-event normally not occurring and limits equivalence with presque; tests form and interpretation.

entries.source_title: Using "si" + L'Imparfait in hypothetical sentences with Le Conditionnel Présent
entries.evidence: Teaches imagined present/future si-imparfait plus conditional, reversed clause order and s'il, contrasts open present-plus-future conditions, and limits the no-conditional-after-si rule to conditional if rather than whether.

entries.source_title: Rappeler [à quelqu'un] = to remind [someone] in French
entries.evidence: Explains rappeler something à someone, recipient lui/leur and rappeler à someone de do something; distinguishes call back and se rappeler, with complete present spelling and targeted constructions.

entries.source_title: Qui = Who/which/that (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Defines antecedent and subject function, explicitly allows people and things, keeps qui before vowels and agrees its verb with the antecedent; exercises test subject choice and plural agreement.

entries.source_title: Que = Whom/which/that (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Defines direct-object function, contrasts it with subject qui, teaches qu' and non-omission, and notes preceding-object participle agreement; exercises include constructing a complete relative sentence.

entries.source_title: En can replace de + [phrase] (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Covers verb/adjective de complements, origin, retained quantities and placement before the governing infinitive; notes nuanced person reference instead of a universal ban.

entries.source_title: Using neuter pronouns le or l' to refer to previously mentioned ideas (French Direct Object Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Explains invariant neutral le for whole facts rather than the noun mentioned inside them, with l' before a vowel and compound placement; items deliberately use feminine/plural facts.

entries.source_title: Y can replace à + [thing/object/location] (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Covers locations and suitable à-idea complements, contrasts person constructions lui versus à lui, and tests placement in simple, compound-negative and infinitive groups.

entries.source_title: Celui/celle/ceux/celles = the one(s) (French Demonstrative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Teaches all four gender/number forms and required identifying de/relative/-ci/-là complements; tasks cover all four forms plus hyphenated celui-ci.

entries.source_title: Certain(e)s d'entre eux/elles = Some of them (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Shows certains/certaines d'entre eux/elles with masculine/mixed and feminine groups, extends to nous, and tests the d'entre link and both agreement decisions.

entries.source_title: Using French adverbial pronoun "y" in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.evidence: Provides vas-y/allons-y/allez-y and explains hyphenation plus linking s when y directly follows a vowel-ending tu command; learners transform place and à-idea complements.

entries.source_title: Using French adverbial pronoun "en" in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.evidence: Teaches attached en, retained quantities, added s including aies-en, moi-to-m' and toi-to-t' elision, and the contrasting infinitive-bound Va en chercher; items separately exercise each distinction.

entries.source_title: L'un(e) ... l'autre/Les un(e)s ... les autres = One ... the other(s) (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Distinguishes pairs from divided larger groups, masculine/feminine forms and reciprocal use with required prepositions; tasks construct l'une, les unes and les unes aux autres.

entries.source_title: Using neuter pronoun le to replace adjectives (French Direct Object Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Neutral le/l' replaces descriptions after être without agreeing with feminine/plural subjects; constructed tasks include l'êtes, a female speaker and future le serons.

entries.source_title: Où can mean where AND when (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Teaches spatial and temporal antecedents, distinguishes où from ou and direct-object que after a place noun, and corrects relative quand after année; items require both spatial and temporal choices.

entries.source_title: Ce qui (vs ce que) = what/which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Explains neutral ce when no noun is named and subject qui, including reference to an entire preceding event; learners identify the subject of plaît/manque/laisse.

entries.source_title: Ce que (vs ce qui) = what/which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Explains ce que as the unnamed direct object when a separate subject follows, including ce qu' before a vowel; exercises use demander and chercher with explicit subjects.

entries.source_title: Ne ... nulle part = Nowhere (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Teaches nulle part as a negative place expression rather than a subject, including simple and compound placement and fragment answers; tests replacement of quelque part.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas = Not - with reflexive verbs in compound tenses (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Displays every reflexive negative person, places ne before pronoun-plus-auxiliary and pas after the auxiliary, adds jamais and notes agreement limits; tasks transform complete clauses and assemble groups.

entries.source_title: Position of French object and adverbial pronouns in negative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.evidence: Restores ordinary preverbal pronoun order, moi-to-me and linking-s removal, covers y/en and two objects, and tests complete affirmative-to-negative transformations.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif) - negative commands
entries.evidence: Gives all tu/nous/vous negative reflexive forms with ne plus te/nous/vous before the verb and pas after it; constructed items prohibit misplaced affirmative toi/hyphens.

entries.source_title: Personne ne ..., rien ne ... = No one, nothing (negation) in French
entries.evidence: Teaches singular subject personne/rien with ne but no pas, compares their distinct object positions, and tests compound negation and singular agreement.

entries.source_title: Using restrictive ne … que to express only with compound tenses (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Places ne before the auxiliary but que directly before the restricted object/time, preserves positive articles, contrasts pas que/not only, and tests elision and scope through full rewrites.

entries.source_title: Aucun/e … ne = None (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Distinguishes adjective/pronoun aucun/aucune, normal singular agreement even before de plus plural, and exceptional plural-only nouns such as frais; exercises include subject and object uses.

entries.source_title: Combining two or more negations (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Explains compatible plus rien, plus jamais, jamais personne and personne...rien with their distinct meanings and compound placement, without a spurious pas or cancellation rule.

entries.source_title: Ni l'un(e) ni l'autre ne ... = Neither (one nor the other) (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Teaches gendered paired subjects with ni and ne but no pas, explicitly accepts singular/plural agreement where both are possible; tasks construct feminine pronouns and accept vient/viennent.

entries.source_title: Omitting the "ne" in informal negative sentences in French (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Pairs informal and careful-written negatives, keeps the remaining negative word, explains register and plus ambiguity, and asks learners to restore ne/n' rather than erase the negation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate paraître/connaître and derivatives (+ avoir) - except apparaître and naître - in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Displays complete connu/paru avoir paradigms and named derivatives, distinguishes naître/apparaître auxiliaries and publication être for paraître; items additionally retrieve méconnu/reparu/comparu. Rare rené is explicitly recognition-only, not a production target.

entries.source_title: Conjugate courir and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Displays all six avoir + couru forms, teaches parcouru/accouru/recouru/secouru and accourir auxiliary variation, and individually tests each named family member without subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif) - affirmative commands
entries.evidence: Provides tu/nous/vous paradigms, subject omission, te-to-toi and hyphenation, and contrasts retained/omitted tu s; constructed items cover all three imperative persons.

entries.source_title: Conjugate battre and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Shows the six-person battu paradigm and combattu/débattu/abattu derivatives, with separate exercises for each; the reflexive se battre task contrasts être and feminine plural battues.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er and -ir verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Displays six-person préparer and finir paradigms, retains silent written e and excludes present -iss-; items vary person and verb, including créer and remplir.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Shows all six ser- forms with aligned translations and future-state examples, contrasts serai/saurai, and tests je, plural noun subject and nous.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Gives all six aur- forms and meaningful future possession/need contexts; exercises include tu, nous and a future quand clause.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Displays ferai/feras/fera/ferons/ferez/feront rather than an infinitive-derived guess; tasks use planning actions with nous, elle and vous.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Shows the complete ir- paradigm and distinguishes simple-future going from present aller and near-future aller plus infinitive; tasks include irai chercher and irez.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -dre and -re verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Explains removing only final e, supplies the complete attendre paradigm and prendre example, and tests répondre, mettre, attendre and prendre without pretending every -re verb is regular.

entries.source_title: Quand/pendant que + future tense (Le Futur Simple) - not the present tense = When/while I do something in the future (Sequence of Tenses in French)
entries.evidence: Uses future inside future quand/pendant que clauses, distinguishes overlapping events, present habits and conditional si, and notes completed-before-future limits; exercises test each contrast.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -éXer, -eXer, -eter, -eler verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Teaches e-to-è in all persons, appeler/jeter doubling, and traditional/revised éXer/-eler/-eter variants from OQLF. Exercises cover every named transfer, including geler/peser/rejeter/compléter, with accepted spelling alternatives.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -oyer/-ayer/-uyer verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Provides complete nettoyer/essuyer/dual-payer paradigms and all endings for the family, distinguishes compulsory i from optional -ayer y, identifies envoyer separately and exercises nettoyer/employer/essuyer/appuyer/payer/essayer.

entries.source_title: Conjugate venir/tenir and derivatives in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Shows all viendr-/tiendr- forms, complete revenir and explicit derivative stems with six endings; exercises apply them to devenir, maintenir, prévenir, obtenir, revenir, soutenir and retenir.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Shows six voudr- forms and future wishes rather than polite conditional requests; items contrast future voudrai spelling and a plural-subject prediction.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Provides the full double-r future paradigm and direct infinitive construction, distinguishes ability from obligation and conditional possibility; exercises retrieve pourrez, pourra and pourront.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Gives all six devr- forms with direct infinitives and obligation contexts while acknowledging expectation readings; exercises distinguish requirement from wish and construct je/nous forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate voir/envoyer in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Displays complete verr-/enverr- paradigms plus revoir/renvoyer, excludes invented envoier-, and contrasts prévoir/pourvoir; exercises now explicitly test both exceptional non-verr- stems as well as core forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate recevoir and other -cevoir verbs in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Shows all recevoir/concevoir persons and the -cevr- derivation for apercevoir, percevoir and décevoir, prohibits a needless cedilla before e, and supplies separate exercises for every named derivative.

entries.source_title: Conjugate most French verbs in the conditional present (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Teaches future stem plus all six conditional endings with complete -er/-ir/-re models, transferred spelling variants and will/would contrast; tasks cover regular and spelling-changing verbs.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Gives serais/serais/serait/serions/seriez/seraient with translated imagined-state contexts and varied subject retrieval.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Displays the complete aur- conditional paradigm, including a meaningful imagined-resource example; items retrieve j'aurais and plural auraient.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the conditional present in French = could (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Shows all six pourr- conditional forms, distinguishes tentative possibilities/requests from past English could, and tests independent requests and conditional consequences.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the conditional present in French = should (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Gives the complete devr- conditional paradigm and advice meaning with direct infinitives, noting context-dependent expectation readings; tasks retrieve tu, plural and nous advice forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Shows all six fer- conditional forms and an imagined work-budget consequence; exercises retrieve feriez in a hypothetical question and ferais in a proposal.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the conditional present in French (Le Conditionnel Présent)
entries.evidence: Provides the complete ir- conditional paradigm, emphasizes irions versus future irons and tests imagined movement with nous and elle.

entries.source_title: Conjugate savoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Shows all six saur- forms, distinguishes know-how from circumstantial ability and saurai from serai; tasks include knowing facts and acquired skill.

entries.source_title: En + "-ant" = While/by + "-ing" in French (Gerund/Le Gérondif)
entries.evidence: Teaches nous-stem formation, ayant/étant/sachant, -ger/-cer spelling, all reflexive persons, invariability, shared subject, means/simultaneity/condition and tout en; varied tasks assess forms, meaning and subject attachment.

entries.source_title: Conjugate valoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Gives vaux/vaux/vaut/valons/valez/valent with value, worthwhile action and il vaut mieux, contrasting price coûter; exercises assess singular/plural forms and phrase meaning.

entries.source_title: Conjugate courir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Displays every courr- future person and contrasts courrons with present courons; exercises test the base plus parcourir, recourir, accourir and secourir with their original meanings.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mourir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Gives all six meur-/mour- forms with literal and clearly figurative uses, distinguishes mourir from tuer, and tests third-person plural, nous, singular and vous stems.

entries.source_title: Conjugate apparaître in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Uses the consulted OQLF auxiliary nuance, teaches customary être without falsely prohibiting avoir, displays all persons and four agreement forms, and constrains tasks to être including polite singular vous.

entries.source_title: Conjugate acquérir and other irregular -QUÉRIR verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.evidence: Shows complete acquérir/conquérir/requérir forms and the reconquérir prefix transfer, limits obsolete quérir to recognition, and exercises the three stem shapes plus named derivatives.

entries.source_title: Which prepositions to use with celebration days - like Christmas - in French
entries.evidence: Teaches à Noël/à Pâques, à la Toussaint and au Nouvel An, contrasts pour and ordinary calendar dates, and acknowledges regional à la Noël while constraining the practiced common forms.

entries.source_title: Expressing distance in French with "à ... de ..." = (at) ... km from ... (French Prepositions)
entries.evidence: Explains à before a measured distance and de before its reference place, including du/d'ici and travel-time distances with a stated mode; exercises test both links and contractions.

entries.source_title: Quelque chose de + [adjectif] = Something [adjective] in French
entries.evidence: Teaches the de/d' link and neutral masculine singular adjective despite ordinary feminine chose, with nouveau/beau and elision tasks plus a full correction.

entries.source_title: Which prepositions to use with name days - like Saint Valentine's Day - in French
entries.evidence: Explains feminine implied fête for à la Saint-Valentin/Patrick/Jean and à la Sainte-Catherine, distinguishing the saint's gender from the feast article and practicing both choices.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the compound past (Le Passé Composé) in French - with nouns
entries.evidence: Retains the noun, repeats it with a matching subject pronoun after the auxiliary, explains inserted -t- versus existing t and formal register; tasks construct complete noun-subject questions.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions with reflexive verbs in the compound past (Le Passé Composé) in French
entries.evidence: Keeps the reflexive pronoun before être while inverting the subject pronoun after it, covers noun subjects and negative questions, and tests se sont-ils, s'est-elle and vous êtes-vous.

entries.source_title: Expressing dimensions and measurements in French (French Numbers)
entries.evidence: Teaches fixed de long/large/haut and depth/diameter terms, mesurer/faire/peser/contenir, natural spoken height, unit genders and decimal conventions; exercises test dimensions without feminine agreement and weight.

entries.source_title: Expressing fractions in French - general (French Numbers)
entries.evidence: Explains numerator/denominator, demi/tiers/quart and ordinal-style fractions with plural marking and de contractions, plus pre-noun demi- versus post-noun et demi(e); tasks retrieve common and general fractions and both half constructions.
